text:
sophia: bringing up reranker-v3-int8 (ptq) on prod rerank bench. quick smoke shows ndcg@10 -0.9% vs fp16, but ndcg@3 -2.4% for short queries (<3 tokens). anyone else seeing short-query skew?

matt: can you paste the eval command + numbers?

sophia: pasted below
```
./eval.py --model reranker-v3-int8 --split prod_holdout --metrics ndcg@3,ndcg@10,mrr
Results:
ndcg@3: 0.412 (-0.010)  # -2.4%
ndcg@10: 0.512 (-0.0046) # -0.9%
mrr: 0.334 (-0.001)
```

ida: candidate generation identical between fp16 and int8?

sophia: yes same candidates, same rerank candidates JSON. doc truncation config identical (512 tokens).

evan: weird. quant shouldn't change ordering much — maybe ties increase due to score quantization?

tanya: slice by query length + judge depth and check tie counts + top-swap rate. also check if any preproc changed (urls, whitespace).

sophia: quick diagnostics: tie_count_top1 +0.8% for int8, bootstrap p ~0.07.

eval-bot: job 2024-12-05T14:22:00Z completed: paired-bootstrap samples=10000, delta(ndcg@3)=-0.0098, p=0.068

matt: p=0.068 is borderline. run paired bootstrap on depth>=10 only.

sophia: ran that slice this morning:
```
slice: depth>=10, n_queries=14000
ndcg@3 delta = -0.002 (p=0.42)
ndcg@10 delta = -0.005 (p=0.12)
```

ida: implies effect concentrated on shallow-judged queries and short queries. might be formatting differences (leading/trailing whitespace, url tokens, casing).

tanya: also check input concat format — did v3 change how we insert <sep>? e.g. `query <sep> doc` vs `query

 doc` can change tokenization.

evan: plus small score perturbations can flip near-equal candidates — check top-1 swap rate and produce a human sample of swaps.

sophia: running two ablations tonight: (1) token normalization (lowercase, collapse spaces, strip/normalize URLs), (2) softmax temperature clamp (temp=1.02) to reduce rounding-induced ties. will post numbers.

matt: also capture candidate score distribution histograms (before/after quant) and count of identical score bins. if quantized logits cluster, that explains ndcg@3 hit.

sophia: noted. I'll add histograms and top-swap examples (200).

ida: if normalization fixes it, then we avoid retraining or quant pipeline fixes. if not, consider per-layer bias folding or PTQ calibration updates.

tanya: for the human sample, focus on short queries and judge depth <5. those are where we see the regressions.

evan: small reminder: log the seed used for PTQ runs and eval sampling. non-determinism can be sneaky.

sophia: good call — including seeds and docker image hash in follow-up. thanks all :thumbsup:

sophia: will update tomorrow with ablation numbers and a short artifact (top-swap CSV + 200 human checks).

ida: sounds good. thanks for the quick triage.
